question.problem:
$\,$ $P$ is a rectangle and $Q$ is not a square.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P\text{ is a rectangle}\text{ and }Q\text{ is not a square}) & ≡¬((P\text{ is a rectangle})∧(Q\text{ is not a square})) \\  & ≡¬(P\text{ is a rectangle})∨¬(Q\text{ is not a square}) \\  & ≡(P\text{ is not a rectangle})∨(Q\text{ is a square}) \\  & ≡P\text{ is not a rectangle}\text{ or }Q\text{ is a square}.\end{aligned}
$$
